description: This office within the Higher Teacher Training College (HTTC) at the University of Bamenda is located to the right immediately after the HTTC Student's Association. The entrance is marked by carved plants along the climb toward the building, and an old notice board stands nearby. The office has two distinct doors, each leading to different services. On the first door, you will find the HTTC Service of Students Affairs and Examination Service for Admissions, Records, and Statistics. Offices here include: Head of Service Students Affairs and Examinations (HOS SAE), Head of Service Admissions, Records, and Statistics (HOS ARS), Secretariat, and Archiving Room. This section also covers HTTC ENS Admission and Students Record, Students Affairs, and Examination. On the second door, you will find the HTTC Division of Counseling and Orientation and the Department of Computer Sciences. Offices here include: Head of Service Internship and Cooperation, Head of Service Orientation, Head of Department Counseling and Orientation (HOD Counseling and Orientation), Student Counselor, and Head of Department Computer Science (HOD Computer Science). Together, these offices provide administrative, academic, and student support services, making the building a key functional landmark within HTTC. To the right of this building is the Directorate of Students Affairs Disabilities Service, identified by a signboard in front. In front of this structure stands a solar pole and a small signboard that reads 'Wheelchair Access – Please Do Not Park Here.' This building also has two distinct doors: the right door is marked HTTC Department of Economics, while the left door is marked HTTTC (Higher Technical Teacher Training College). The Department of Economics focuses on economic theory, policy, and applied studies, while HTTTC provides specialized training in technical and vocational education within the University of Bamenda. Moving further to the right, you will find the HTTTC/ENSET Secretary General's Office. This building is identified by a white signboard with light blue writing in front of it. The structure is built of stone and painted white, giving it a solid and clean appearance. It has two distinct doors: the right door leads to the English Modern Letters Department, while the left door leads to the Division of Training and Orientation. These offices contribute to academic coordination, language studies, and orientation services within HTTTC/ENSET. Still further to the right is the Directorate of Higher Technical Teacher Training College Bambili. The signboard in front identifies the offices housed here, including the Office of the Director, the Office of the Secretary General, and the Division of Administration and Finance. The building is equally made of stones, but unlike the Secretary General's Office, its stones are painted black. It also features a wooden entrance, giving it a distinctive appearance among the HTTTC landmarks.

description: The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Bamenda is located to the right of the Directorate of Higher Technical Teacher Training College. The Faculty Office manages student records, faculty coordination, and administrative services. To the right side of Hall 5 on the second floor is the Dean's Secretariat, which provides leadership and oversight for the Faculty of Health Sciences. On the campus, there is also the Faculty of Health Sciences Association, a student body organization, and its building is painted blue. Together, these halls, offices, and the association make the Faculty of Health Sciences a central academic and administrative landmark within the University of Bamenda.

description: AMPHI 340 at the University of Bamenda is located directly in front of the Faculty of Health Sciences halls. The building serves as a large classroom and amphitheater for lectures and gatherings. On its right side, there are glass notice boards used for posting information and announcements. At the same level as these notice boards, there is a signboard that reads 'Higher Technical Teacher Training College Student's Association,' marking its connection to student activities. AMPHI 340 is a central academic class space within the campus, positioned prominently opposite the Faculty of Health Sciences halls. Moving further to the right, you will find the SOA classes SOA 1 and SOA 2. These two classes are built of stone and painted white. Behind SOA 1 and 2 is the HTTTC/ENSET Department of Social Economy and Family Management, option Home Economics, housed in a building with dark glass windows. On the first door here is this department, while moving to the right on the second door you will find the HTTTC Service in charge of Sports. The next door houses the HTTTC Head of Service in charge of Business and Innovation, and on that same door also the HTTTC Head of Service in charge of Maintenance. The following door is the HTTTC Department of Renewable Energy, headed by the HOD. Continuing to the right, attached to these offices are additional classes: SOA 12 and SOA 13, which face directly opposite SOA 15 and SOA 14. A wooden staircase stands directly in front of SOA 13. This staircase is the key access point: descending it leads you to the lower level where the sequence of SOA halls continues, specifically SOA 4 through SOA 11. Note: when you are behind SOA 1 and 2, you will see this arrangement of departments and classes. If you are on the school road, you will see SOA 1 and 2, and going down you will notice a wooden entrance. In front of this entrance is a small signboard painted light blue and white, reading 'HTTTC-ENSET Junior Enterprise Offices,' with an arrow pointing toward the wooden staircase. Taking this staircase leads you back behind SOA 1 and 2, where the departments and offices described above are located, and further down into the alignment of SOA halls.

description: The Second Gate of the University of Bamenda is located after descending from the main gate. It regulates entry and is marked by barrier poles painted in alternating white and red. Directly facing the Second Gate is the Amazing Grace Bakery, a place where food and snacks are available. While entering through the Second Gate, to your left you will see a building made up of small blocks. In front of this building there is a blackboard and a small placard. The placard reads 'UBa Ventures Canteen – Food is Ready,' while the blackboard displays 'UBa Venture PLC Canteen Menu.' The menu listed includes traditional dishes such as ekwang, white beans, and fried plantain. Moving further along the same line, you will see a building made of stones painted white known as the Computer Center. This facility has two doors and serves as a hub for computing and digital services. Still moving forward, another stone building painted white appears, with a signboard in front reading 'University of Bamenda Directorate of Development, Physical Plans and Infrastructure (DPPI).' Within this building are the Office of the Director, the Development Division, the Physical Plant Division, and the Maintenance Division. The entrance is marked by beautifully arranged trees, and the facility has two doors. Continuing forward, you will bypass these and pass a black notice board before reaching another building made of stone but painted black: the COLTECH office. In front of this office is a green signboard displaying information in both French and English. It includes the COLTECH logo, the name of the school (COLTECH), and details of degree programs. The entrance is decorated with beautifully carved plants and trees, and in front of the office there is a chair for visitors to wait. The facility has two doors. Facing the building, the left door leads to the Directorate of COLTECH. A blue signboard here reads 'Directorate of COLTECH (College of Technology),' listing offices such as the Office of the Director, Office of the Director of Studies, Office of the Secretary General, Division of Admission and Records, and Division of Administration and Finance. Directly behind this office is the College of Technology Student Association (COSTA). Joined to COSTA is AMPHI 50, constructed by the COLTECH Student Association. Descending further from this area leads to the field where students play football.

description: The football field of the University of Bamenda lies below the COLTECH Student's Association (COSTA) as you descend, with the COLTECH office positioned in front and COSTA directly behind it. Opposite the football field stands the PBA classroom block. In front of PBA there is a green notice board inscribed 'Done by HTTC (ENS) Students Association 2014/2015.' The building has two floors: on the ground floor are classrooms PBA 01 to PBA 06, and on the second floor is classroom PBA 07. Directly opposite PBA 07 are offices for the Department of Bilingual Letters (left door) and the Department of Philosophy (right door). Slightly behind the PBA block is the Higher Technical Teachers Training College (HTTTC), also called the PBB block. It has two floors. On the ground floor are classrooms PBB 01 to PBB 06, and directly opposite PBB 05 are offices for the Head of Department of Crop Production Technology, the Head of Department of Agribusiness Technology, and the Head of Department of Computer Engineering. On the second floor are classrooms PBB 07 and PBB 08; directly opposite these classrooms are offices for the Department of Forestry and Wildlife Technology, the Department of Food and Bio-Resource Technology, and the Department of Agricultural and Environmental Engineering. Below the football field, there is a small entrance to the left. At the beginning of this entrance stands a white signboard with 'Faculty of Education' written on it. Under that are 'Vice Dean in charge of Programming and Academic Affairs (VD/PAA)' and 'Faculty Officers (FO).' Taking this entrance leads to the LC (Lower Campus) classrooms, ranging from LC 01 to LC 10. LC 10 is joined to the Biology Laboratory. At the top left of the Biology Laboratory is the Geology Laboratory. The sign on the Geology Laboratory is faint and difficult to read. On this same building(Geology Laboratory), which stands in front of the Biology Laboratory but to its left, there is also a notice board and another door without labeling.

description: Also known as Block 17, the CCAST Block is reached by passing the School Restaurant and descending the road to the left. As you go down, you will immediately recognize the CCAST field on your left. The field is spacious and features a prominent statue shaped like the map of Cameroon, as well as a grandstand area with multiple steps for seating during events. On your right, you will see small fenced sports courts, including basketball and possibly volleyball courts. Continue descending to the end, then turn left.
